question: A team designed its Claude-assisted case-note arrangement around one unusually clean example case, and it worked perfectly. They now plan to put all case types through it. What is the greatest risk?
options: A) Claude will produce case notes that are noticeably longer than the previous ones
B) The arrangement was tuned to a case that does not represent the messy real ones
C) Colleagues will find the written instructions too long to read before using it
D) The team will exceed its weekly usage allowance within the first fortnight of use
correct_answers: B) The arrangement was tuned to a case that does not represent the messy real ones
explanations: Note length is a formatting matter that a reviewer would spot immediately and can be specified away.

Correct. A design validated on one tidy case has been fitted to the easiest conditions it will ever face. The awkward, incomplete and contested cases are where it will fail, and none of them was tested.
Instruction length is a usability nuisance that is easy to notice and easy to shorten.
Allowance pressure is a manageable operational cost, and it would show up plainly rather than producing quietly wrong case notes.
